column1: # Hand-checked segmentations, used as a regression set for the segmenter.
# Deliberately NOT derived from `word_decompositions`: that table is itself
# produced by running `segment()` over the sources' example words, so scoring
# against it would only measure the segmenter's agreement with itself.
# Segments are reported under the CANONICAL morpheme id, which is not always
# how the word spells it: `unbelievable` is `un` + `believe` + `able`, not
# `believ`. Every id here must resolve in the morpheme table.
# Lines beginning with GAP are words this pass is known NOT to handle, kept
# here so the reason stays recorded and so a future pass can measure progress.
# Their stated cause is in the trailing comment.
# Both upstream sources are Greek/Latin BOUND-root dictionaries, so the
# Germanic core of English was missing outright and nothing built on it could
# be segmented at all. Supplied by the curated native-stem entries in data/sources/morphemes.json.
# The stem is in the table under its canonical spelling; the word spells it
# differently because a productive rule applied at the morpheme boundary.
# Reversed by crates/analyzer/src/ortho.rs, NOT enumerated per stem in the
# data — these rules apply to stems the table has never seen.
# No spelling rule predicts these, so they live in the stem's `variants`.
# Note admission is `admit` + `-ion`, NOT `ad-` + `admit` + `-ion` as an
# earlier draft of this file had it: segments have to tile the word, and
# `admiss` is the surface spelling of `admit`, with the `ad-` already in it.
# Words this pass still cannot reach, kept so the reason stays recorded and a
# Inflection has no owner in this engine: there is no lemmatization step, so
# `-s` and `-ed` are deliberately not treated as suffixes (see
# FINAL_ONE_CHAR_SUFFIXES in segment.rs). These need that step, not more data.
# Ablaut and suppletion rewrite the vowel, not the spelling around it. No
# orthographic rule reaches them and they are irregular per verb, so they
# A curated variant losing to a chain of noisy upstream affixes. `deception`
# parses as dec- + ept + -ion, because ROOT_START pays 8/char to push the root
# rightward and both `dec` and `ept` are labelled forms in the source data, so
# the junk parse scores 27 against 14 for the true `deceive` + `-ion`.
# Its near-twin `reception` only survives because `rec` happens not to be
# labelled a prefix upstream — the difference is data noise, not analysis.
# Fixing it means either weighting curated variants above source affixes or
# pruning the affix inventory; both are their own pass.
